title: Use a static method reference `Integer::parseInt` to convert a list of string numbers to integers.
shortTitle: Use a static method reference Integer::parseInt to convert a list of string numbers to integers
keyPoints: Integer::parseInt is a static method reference matching Function<String, Integer> or ToIntFunction<String>
Use map(Integer::parseInt) for Stream<Integer> or mapToInt(Integer::parseInt) for primitive IntStream
mapToInt avoids autoboxing and gives access to sum(), average(), and other numeric operations
parseInt throws NumberFormatException on malformed input, aborting the entire stream
In production, wrap parsing in a helper returning Optional and filter empties to handle dirty data
Static references have no receiver object: the argument is passed directly to the static method

s1_definition.oneliner: Integer::parseInt is a static method reference that parses each numeric string into an int when used in map or mapToInt.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Integer::parseInt** references the static method `parseInt(String)` as a functional value.
- Matches `Function<String, Integer>` (for map) or `ToIntFunction<String>` (for mapToInt).
- **mapToInt** produces a primitive IntStream for efficient numeric aggregation.
- **NumberFormatException** on malformed input aborts the stream.
- No receiver object is involved: the argument goes directly to the static method.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya at the National Bank of India receives transaction amounts as text and needs them as numbers to add up. Instead of writing 'take the text and parse it', she points at the built-in parse tool and runs each text through it.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Stream<String>   ["100", "250", "75", "300"]
       │
       │  .mapToInt(Integer::parseInt)
       │
       │  Static method: no receiver
       │  Each string → Integer.parseInt(string) → int
       ▼
  IntStream [100, 250, 75, 300]  (primitive, no boxing)
       │
       │  .sum()
       ▼
  int: 725
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A static method reference passes the argument directly to the static method with no receiver. Integer::parseInt matches a function from String to int, so mapToInt(Integer::parseInt) parses each numeric string into a primitive int and produces an IntStream ready for sum(), average(), and other numeric operations.

The critical production concern is error handling. parseInt throws NumberFormatException on malformed input, and a method reference has no room for a try-catch, so one bad record aborts the entire stream. At the National Bank of India, the transaction import wrapped parsing in a helper returning OptionalInt and filtered out failures.

Use mapToInt for primitive efficiency and numeric aggregation; use map for Stream<Integer> when you need collect operations.

Remember one sentence: Integer::parseInt is a static method reference for parsing strings to ints, and in production always guard against NumberFormatException.
